rule_evaluation_trace.condition: An SCONJ in the configured clause-subordinator list is flagged when any of: it is the sentence ROOT (unattached marker); it has a mark dependency but its head is not a parser-labeled clause predicate; it has a mark dependency and its head is the sentence's only finite ROOT clause predicate (suppressed when a separate finite subordinate-clause predicate with its own subject is also observed, indicating likely marker misattachment); it has a prep dependency with no pobj/obj complement; or it is 'because' attached as prep with only a nominal pobj and no later predicate.
rule_evaluation_trace.configuration: Gate: token POS is SCONJ and text in CLAUSE_SUBORDINATORS={'although','as','because','before','if','once','since','though','unless','until','when','whereas','while'}. Flag if any of five OR conditions: (1) dependency == 'ROOT'; (2) dependency == 'mark' and head_start not in predicate_starts (VERB/AUX with CLAUSE_DEPENDENCIES); (3) dependency == 'mark' and head_start is the sentence's only finite ROOT predicate (head_is_only_root_clause: VERB/AUX, tag in FINITE_TAGS={'VB','VBD','VBP','VBZ'}, dependency 'ROOT', sole such root); condition (3) is suppressed when the sentence also contains a separate finite subordinate-clause predicate (dependency in {'advcl','ccomp','xcomp'}, tag in FINITE_TAGS) with its own parser-labeled subject, indicating the marker's ROOT attachment is likely a parser misattachment and the two-clause structure is already observed; (4) dependency == 'prep' with no pobj/obj child and no prep child that itself has a pobj/obj; (5) marker == 'because', dependency == 'prep', pobj child (text != 'of') present, and no predicate starts after the marker's end. Parser attachment can be wrong; this is an observation, not proof.
